text:
maria: Heads-up: SCIM provisioning is failing for ~200 Okta users in the last hour. Lots of duplicate-email conflicts and KMS decrypt denies. Provisioner is spamming errors and customers are seeing missing accounts. Anyone oncall for the provisioner or KMS IAM?

samir: I'm on it — can you paste the exact error you're seeing? Also which IdP (Okta / Azure AD)?

maria: Okta. Log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z provisioner ERROR scim.apply batch_id=8423 user=alice@example.com create failed: 409 duplicate attribute (email)
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z provisioner ERROR scim.user sync failed user=alice@example.com err="unknown_user: externalId missing"
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z kms WARN decrypt failed status=403 alias=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/provisioner/cryptoKeys/prov-key-1 err="PermissionDenied"
```
Also see a flurry of 403s in the KMS audit around 14:01-14:05.

devon: We rotated the prov-key-1 key material during maintenance yesterday. Did we update the key's IAM binding to include the provisioner service account? If the key was re-created or a new version deployed, the alias might point to a new key that doesn't grant the provisioner SA crypto.decrypt.

kevin: @devon that was my change — I did a key rotation but I thought IAM came along. Checking now. In the meantime you can confirm by checking the provisioner pod env var KMS_KEY_ALIAS and the SA bound to it:
```
kubectl -n infra get deploy scim-provisioner -o yaml | grep -i KMS_KEY_ALIAS
kubectl -n infra describe sa scim-provisioner-sa
```
If the SA isn't in key IAM, add roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter for that principal.

anna-sec: Can someone link the KMS admin audit log for the 14:00 window? Need it for the incident timeline. Also, are duplicate-email events correlated with Okta SCIM retries or with a separate RBAC migration we ran this morning?

ops-bot: <https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query;query=resource.type%3D%22k8s_container%22%20protoPayload.methodName%3D%22google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt%22%20timestamp%3D%222026-03-18T14:00:00Z..2026-03-18T14:10:00Z%22|KMS decrypt log slice>

samir: From the apps audit we see two things: 1) Okta sent a batch that included two users with the same email (legacy importer + normal SCIM user), which causes 409s and leaves the local DB in a partially-applied state. 2) After the DB partial state, the provisioner tries to re-sync and hits decrypt on a blob stored with the old key version -> 403 when key policy changed.

devon: Mitigations:
- Short: Re-add scim-provisioner-sa to prov-key-1 IAM with cryptoKeyDecrypter so existing decrypts succeed.
- Medium: Run a controlled SCIM backfill fixing duplicate externalIds in Okta for the affected tenants (script attached below).
- Long: Update provisioner to handle missing externalId gracefully (audit event) and to retry with fallback decrypt key if configured.

devon: backfill script (quick and dirty):
```
# find dup emails in okta for tenant X
python tools/okta_find_dups.py --tenant=acme-corp --output=dups.json
# fix: pick primary by okta.createdAt, patch others externalId=add-suffix
python tools/okta_patch_externalid.py --dups=dups.json --strategy=append-suffix
# then re-run scim backfill job
kubectl -n infra run scim-backfill --image=redwood/tools:latest --command -- /bin/sh -c "python backfill.py --tenant=acme-corp"
```

maria: I don't love the append-suffix approach as a general rule, but we need something low-risk to unblock. Can we do this per-tenant and run in canary (tenant acme-corp -> 50 users) first?

kevin: I'm adding the SA binding now. Will notify when done. If IAM fix works, we should see decrypt 200s and the queue should shrink.

anna-sec: Also open an audit ticket for the RBAC change (who rotated keys and why). We need the decision trail. @kevin please include the change CL/PR and the time you applied it.

samir: If anyone hits a tenant with many 409s, prefer manual reconcile over the bulk backfill. Our DB partial-state cleanup is delicate. I'll standby to approve manual fixes.

maria: Action items:
- kevin: revert/add KMS IAM binding (in progress) -> update thread when done
- devon: prepare safe canary backfill for acme-corp (50 users)
- samir: stand by for manual reconciliation for high-risk tenants
- anna-sec: create incident record and collect audit logs
I'll open an incident in PagerDuty and add links. Thanks team :thumbsup: 

kevin: IAM binding added at 14:12 UTC. Provisioner logs now show:
```
2026-03-18T14:12:45Z kms INFO decrypt succeeded alias=... user=alice@example.com
2026-03-18T14:12:50Z provisioner INFO scim.apply batch_id=8423 user=alice@example.com retry succeeded
```
Queue size dropped from ~5k -> 120 in 20m.

maria: Great. Keep monitoring for a couple hours. Devon, let's schedule the canary backfill at 16:00 UTC. Anna-sec, please attach the audit links in the incident ticket. I'll follow up with a postmortem template after we stabilize.
